records.source: בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י לְצֵ֥את בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה בָּ֖אוּ מִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי׃
records.gloss: In the month the third of [the] going out of [the] sons of Israel from [the] land of Egypt, on the day the this they came [to the] wilderness of Sinai.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} arrived in the wilderness of Sinai on the day the third month began after their departure from the land of Egypt.

L.1: In the third month of the going out of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from the land of Egypt, on this day they came [to] the wilderness of Sinai.

R.1: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} reached the Desert of Sinai at the start of the third month after they left Egypt.

decisions.choice: in the third month ... on this day: on the first day of the third month
alternatives: in the third month ... on that same day (with no exact day given)
decisions.reason: The word for "month" also means "new moon", the day a month begins. "On this day" then points to that day: the new moon of the third month after leaving Egypt. Israel left on the fifteenth day of the first month (12:6, 31; Numbers 33:3), so about six weeks had passed.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Sinai: the desert land around Mount Sinai
decisions.reason: The name covers the wild land around the mountain where Israel will camp until Numbers 10:11-12. The mountain is the place where God met Moses in the bush (3:1, 12), there called Horeb.

decisions.choice: Desert of Sinai
decisions.reason: Readable says "desert" for "wilderness", as it says "Desert of Sin" (16:1; 17:1).

records.heading: Israel at Mount Sinai

records.source: וַיִּסְע֣וּ מֵרְפִידִ֗ים וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ מִדְבַּ֣ר סִינַ֔י וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַיִּֽחַן־שָׁ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נֶ֥גֶד הָהָֽר׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Rephidim and they came [to the] wilderness of Sinai and they encamped in the wilderness, and encamped there Israel before the mountain.
pieces: They had moved on from Rephidim and come into the wilderness of Sinai, and there in the wilderness they set up camp. Israel camped there, facing the mountain.

L.2: And they set out from Rephidim and came [to] the wilderness of Sinai, and they camped in the wilderness; and Israel camped there before the mountain.

R.2: They had left Rephidim and come into the Desert of Sinai. They set up camp there in the desert, with Israel's tents facing the mountain.

decisions.choice: Israel camped: the whole people as one
decisions.reason: After the plural "they camped", the verse switches to a singular verb with "Israel" as its subject. The people camp as one body before the mountain, ready for what God will do there.

decisions.choice: before the mountain: the mountain of God
decisions.reason: "The mountain" needs no name: it is the mountain of God where Moses was told that Israel would serve God (3:1, 12). That promise is now being kept.

decisions.choice: with Israel's tents facing the mountain
decisions.reason: Readable turns "Israel camped there before the mountain" into a picture of the camp's tents facing it; the sense is the same.

records.source: וּמֹשֶׁ֥ה עָלָ֖ה אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֵלָ֤יו יְהוָה֙ מִן־הָהָ֣ר לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֤ה תֹאמַר֙ לְבֵ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְתַגֵּ֖יד לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And Moses went up to the God, and called to him Yahweh from the mountain saying, thus you will say to [the] house of Jacob and you will tell to [the] sons of Israel,
pieces: Moses went up to God, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called out to him from the mountain: "Say this to the house of Jacob, and declare it to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}:

L.3: And Moses went up to God, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called to him from the mountain, saying, "Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob and tell to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel:

R.3: Moses went up the mountain to meet with God. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} called to him from the mountain and said, "Here is what you must tell the family of Jacob, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}:

decisions.choice: Moses went up to God ... from the mountain: Moses climbs toward God, who calls to him from the mountain
decisions.reason: Moses goes up toward the place where God is present, and God speaks to him from the mountain before he reaches the top. This is the first of several climbs in chapters 19-24.

decisions.choice: the house of Jacob ... the sons of Israel: the same people, named twice
decisions.reason: The two names stand in parallel, as in poetry. "House of Jacob" recalls the family that went down to Egypt (1:1); "sons of Israel" is the people as a nation. The words that follow are formal and carefully shaped.

decisions.choice: went up the mountain to meet with God
decisions.reason: Readable says where Moses went and why. The Hebrew has "went up to God".

records.source: אַתֶּ֣ם רְאִיתֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי לְמִצְרָ֑יִם וָאֶשָּׂ֤א אֶתְכֶם֙ עַל־כַּנְפֵ֣י נְשָׁרִ֔ים וָאָבִ֥א אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: You you have seen what I did to Egypt, and I carried you on wings of eagles and I brought you to myself.
pieces: 'You saw with your own eyes what I did to the Egyptians, and how I lifted you up on eagles' wings and brought you here to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.4: 'You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and [how] I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}.

R.4: 'You saw what I did to the Egyptians. I carried you along the way an eagle carries its young on its wings, and I brought you here to be with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: carried you on eagles' wings: God bore Israel safely and with strength
decisions.reason: The picture is of a great bird carrying its young. Deuteronomy 32:11-12 uses the same picture of the LORD guiding Israel through the wilderness. It speaks of God's power and care in bringing them out of Egypt and through the desert.

decisions.choice: eagles: large birds of prey, perhaps vultures
decisions.reason: The word names a large bird of prey. It can include the griffon vulture (Micah 1:16 speaks of its bald head). The point is the bird's size, strength and swift flight, not which bird it is.

decisions.choice: brought you to myself: God's goal was not only freedom but nearness to him
decisions.reason: The exodus was not only an escape from Egypt. God brought the people to the mountain where he is present, to belong to him and serve him (3:12; 6:7).

decisions.choice: the way an eagle carries its young
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture as a comparison, following Deuteronomy 32:11. "To be with me" spells out "to myself".

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה אִם־שָׁמ֤וֹעַ תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ בְּקֹלִ֔י וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֑י וִהְיִ֨יתֶם לִ֤י סְגֻלָּה֙ מִכָּל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים כִּי־לִ֖י כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And now, if surely you will listen to my voice and you will keep my covenant, and you will be to me a possession from all the peoples, for to me [is] all the earth.
pieces: So now, if you truly listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice and hold to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, then of all the peoples you will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own special treasure. The whole earth belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},

L.5: And now, if you will surely listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, you will be to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a special possession out of all the peoples, for all the earth [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

R.5: So now, if you really listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, you will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own special treasure out of all the peoples. That is because the whole earth is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}},

decisions.choice: if you will surely listen to my voice: if you will truly obey me
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. To "listen to the voice" of someone is to do what they say (15:26; Deuteronomy 13:5). The promise that follows rests on Israel's keeping the covenant.

decisions.choice: possession: a personal treasure, specially owned and valued
decisions.reason: The word is used of a king's own store of treasure (1 Chronicles 29:3; Ecclesiastes 2:8). God uses it of Israel in Deuteronomy 7:6, 14:2 and 26:18, and Malachi 3:17 and 1 Peter 2:9 take it up. Israel belongs to God in a special way, though all peoples are his.

decisions.choice: for all the earth is mine: a reason, or a contrast
alternatives: although all the earth is mine
decisions.reason: The joining word usually means "for" or "because": God, who owns the whole earth, is free to choose one people as his own. It can also be read as "although": though the whole earth is his, Israel will be his in a special way. Both readings stress that Israel's place is God's choice, not their own claim.

decisions.choice: my own special treasure
decisions.reason: The word means property that is especially prized; "own special treasure" brings out both ownership and value. Literal has "special possession".

records.source: וְאַתֶּ֧ם תִּהְיוּ־לִ֛י מַמְלֶ֥כֶת כֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְג֣וֹי קָד֑וֹשׁ אֵ֚לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And you you will be to me a kingdom of priests and a nation holy. These [are] the words which you will speak to [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: and you will be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation that belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.' These are the words you are to speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."

L.6: And you yourselves will be to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.' These [are] the words that you shall speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel."

R.6: and you will be a kingdom of priests who serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, a nation set apart for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.' Tell these words to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."

decisions.choice: a kingdom of priests: a people who all serve God as priests do
decisions.reason: A priest stands near God, serves him and brings others near to him. The whole people is to belong to God in this way and stand between him and the other peoples of the earth, whom he also owns (verse 5). 1 Peter 2:9 and Revelation 1:6 and 5:10 apply the words to the people of Christ.

decisions.choice: a holy nation: a nation set apart to belong to God
decisions.reason: "Holy" means set apart for God and marked by his character (Leviticus 11:44; 19:2). The word for "nation" is the one used of other peoples; Israel is a people among the nations but set apart from them.

decisions.choice: these are the words: the message Moses is to carry ends here
decisions.reason: The phrase closes the message begun in verse 3. Verses 7-8 tell how Moses passed it on and how the people answered.

decisions.choice: who serve me ... set apart for me
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what being priests and being holy means here. The Hebrew has "to me" once, covering both phrases.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣א מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֖א לְזִקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וַיָּ֣שֶׂם לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And came Moses and he summoned the elders of the people and he set before them all the words the these which he had commanded him Yahweh.
pieces: Moses came back and called the elders of the people together. He laid out for them all these words, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him.

L.7: And Moses came and summoned the elders of the people, and he set before them all these words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him.

R.7: Moses went back and called together the leaders of the people. He told them everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him to say.

decisions.choice: set before them all these words: presented God's offer for their answer
decisions.reason: To "set before" someone is to lay out a choice or a word for them to respond to (Deuteronomy 11:26; 30:15). Moses does not only report; he puts the covenant offer before the people.

decisions.choice: the elders of the people: the leaders who speak for the people
decisions.reason: The elders are the heads of the tribes and families, who represent the whole people (3:16; 4:29; 12:21). Through them the message reaches everyone, and in verse 8 all the people answer.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "elders", as elsewhere in Exodus.

records.source: וַיַּעֲנ֨וּ כָל־הָעָ֤ם יַחְדָּו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה נַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וַיָּ֧שֶׁב מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And answered all the people together and they said, all that has spoken Yahweh we will do. And brought back Moses the words of the people to Yahweh.
pieces: The people answered as one: "We will do everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken." And Moses carried the people's words back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.8: And all the people answered together and said, "All that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken we will do." And Moses brought back the words of the people to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.8: All the people answered together, "We will do all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said." Then Moses went back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} what the people said.

decisions.choice: together: all as one, with one voice
decisions.reason: The word stresses that the answer was shared by the whole people. The same promise is made again when the covenant is sealed (24:3, 7).

decisions.choice: all that Yahweh has spoken we will do: the people accept the covenant offer
decisions.reason: The people agree to the condition of verse 5 before they have heard the laws in full. Their promise will soon be tested (32:1-8).

decisions.choice: brought back the words: reported the answer
decisions.reason: Moses goes between God and the people, carrying God's word to them and their answer back to God.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י בָּ֣א אֵלֶיךָ֮ בְּעַ֣ב הֶֽעָנָן֒ בַּעֲב֞וּר יִשְׁמַ֤ע הָעָם֙ בְּדַבְּרִ֣י עִמָּ֔ךְ וְגַם־בְּךָ֖ יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לְעוֹלָ֑ם וַיַּגֵּ֥ד מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, look I [am] coming to you in [the] thickness of the cloud, so that may hear the people when I speak with you and also in you they will believe forever. And told Moses the words of the people to Yahweh.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Look, I am coming to you in a dark, heavy cloud, so that the people will hear when I speak with you and will trust you from now on." Moses reported the people's words to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Look, I [am] coming to you in the thickness of the cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also believe in you forever." And Moses told the words of the people to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.9: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "I will come to you in a thick, dark cloud. The people will hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} talking with you, and then they will always trust you." Moses passed on the people's answer to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the thickness of the cloud: a dense, dark cloud
decisions.reason: The first word means a thick or dark cloud, so the phrase stresses how dense it is. God comes hidden in it; the people will hear him but not see him (20:21; Deuteronomy 4:11-12).

decisions.choice: also believe in you forever: trust Moses as God's messenger from then on
decisions.reason: Hearing God speak with Moses will show the people that Moses truly speaks for God, so that they rely on his word in later times. After the sea they "believed in the LORD and in Moses his servant" (14:31).

decisions.choice: Moses told the words of the people: a repeated report
decisions.reason: Verse 8 has already said that Moses brought the people's answer back. This may repeat that report as the setting for God's reply, or it may be a second report after God's word in this verse.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֙ לֵ֣ךְ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ֥ם הַיּ֖וֹם וּמָחָ֑ר וְכִבְּס֖וּ שִׂמְלֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, go to the people and you will consecrate them today and tomorrow, and they will wash their clothes,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Go to the people, and today and tomorrow consecrate them. They must wash their clothes

L.10: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments,

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Go to the people. Today and tomorrow, make them holy and ready to meet with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They must wash their clothes

decisions.choice: consecrate them: make them holy, ready to come near God
decisions.reason: To consecrate is to set apart as holy. Here it means preparing the people to be near God's presence: washing their clothes and keeping from sexual relations (verses 14-15; Genesis 35:2; Joshua 3:5).

decisions.choice: wash their clothes: an outward sign of being made ready
decisions.reason: Washing the clothes before meeting God shows that the people are clean and set apart (Genesis 35:2; Leviticus 15). The washing is a sign; the holiness comes from God's call.

decisions.choice: make them holy and ready to meet with me
decisions.reason: Readable explains "consecrate" with its purpose here, which verses 11 and 17 make clear.

records.source: וְהָי֥וּ נְכֹנִ֖ים לַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י כִּ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י יֵרֵ֧ד יְהוָ֛ה לְעֵינֵ֥י כָל־הָעָ֖ם עַל־הַ֥ר סִינָֽי׃
records.gloss: and they will be prepared for the day the third, for on the day the third will come down Yahweh to [the] eyes of all the people on Mount Sinai.
pieces: and be prepared for the third day, for on the third day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will descend upon Mount Sinai with all the people watching.

L.11: and let them be prepared for the third day, for on the third day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come down before the eyes of all the people upon Mount Sinai.

R.11: and be ready on the third day. That is when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come down on Mount Sinai, and all the people will see it.

decisions.choice: the third day: the day after tomorrow
decisions.reason: Counting today as the first day (verse 10), the third day is the day after tomorrow. Verse 16 tells what happened on that day.

decisions.choice: will come down before the eyes of all the people: the people will see the signs of his coming
decisions.reason: The people will see the cloud, the fire and the smoke on the mountain (verses 16-18), but not God himself; they heard a voice and saw no form (Deuteronomy 4:12, 15).

records.source: וְהִגְבַּלְתָּ֤ אֶת־הָעָם֙ סָבִ֣יב לֵאמֹ֔ר הִשָּׁמְר֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם עֲל֥וֹת בָּהָ֖ר וּנְגֹ֣עַ בְּקָצֵ֑הוּ כָּל־הַנֹּגֵ֥עַ בָּהָ֖ר מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
records.gloss: And you will set bounds [for] the people all around saying, take heed to yourselves [of] going up on the mountain and touching its edge. Every one who touches the mountain surely will be put to death.
pieces: Mark out a boundary for the people all the way around, and warn them, 'Watch yourselves! Do not climb the mountain or even touch the edge of it. Anyone who touches the mountain is to be put to death.

L.12: And you shall set bounds for the people all around, saying, 'Guard yourselves [from] going up on the mountain or touching its edge. Everyone who touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.

R.12: Mark a line all around the mountain that the people must not cross. Tell them, 'Be careful! Do not go up the mountain or even touch the bottom of it. Anyone who touches the mountain must be put to death.

decisions.choice: set bounds for the people all around: mark a limit around the mountain that the people may not pass
decisions.reason: The verb means to set a border. The limit keeps the people back; in verse 23 Moses speaks of it as setting bounds for the mountain itself. Both are true: the line runs around the mountain and holds the people off.

decisions.choice: its edge: the lowest slopes, the foot of the mountain
decisions.reason: The word means the end or edge of something. Here it is the place where the mountain begins. Even touching it is forbidden while God is present on it.

decisions.choice: shall surely be put to death: the mountain is holy while God is on it
decisions.reason: The doubled verb is the form used in the law for the death penalty (21:12). The mountain has become holy ground (3:5), and crossing the limit is treated as a capital offense.

decisions.choice: a line all around the mountain that the people must not cross
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "set bounds for the people all around" means.

records.source: לֹא־תִגַּ֨ע בּ֜וֹ יָ֗ד כִּֽי־סָק֤וֹל יִסָּקֵל֙ אוֹ־יָרֹ֣ה יִיָּרֶ֔ה אִם־בְּהֵמָ֥ה אִם־אִ֖ישׁ לֹ֣א יִחְיֶ֑ה בִּמְשֹׁךְ֙ הַיֹּבֵ֔ל הֵ֖מָּה יַעֲל֥וּ בָהָֽר׃
records.gloss: Not will touch him a hand, for surely he will be stoned or surely he will be shot; whether beast or man, not he will live. When sounds long the ram's horn, they will go up on the mountain.
pieces: No one is to lay a hand on such a person; that one must be stoned or shot with arrows. Whether it is an animal or a human being, it must not live.' When the ram's horn sounds a long note, they may go up on the mountain."

L.13: No hand shall touch him, for he shall surely be stoned or surely be shot; whether beast or {{gender:human|man}}, he shall not live.' When the ram's horn sounds long, they shall go up on the mountain."

R.13: Do not touch that person. Kill them with stones or arrows from a distance. That goes for animals as well as people. They must not live.' When the ram's horn blows a long blast, they may go up on the mountain."

decisions.choice: no hand shall touch him: the offender is to be killed from a distance
alternatives: no hand shall touch it (the mountain)
decisions.reason: Those who carry out the sentence must not cross the limit or lay hands on the one who has, so he is stoned or shot with arrows from outside. The word "him" could also be read "it", the mountain: no hand is to touch the mountain.

decisions.choice: the ram's horn: a horn blown as a signal
decisions.reason: The word is used of the horns blown at Jericho (Joshua 6:4-6) and gives its name to the year of jubilee (Leviticus 25:10). A long blast is the signal that the time of danger is over.

decisions.choice: they shall go up on the mountain: the people may then come up
alternatives: they may come up to the mountain
decisions.reason: "They" are most likely the people: after the signal they may go up on the mountain, or up to it. It could also mean only those chosen to go up, as in 24:1, 9. The Hebrew can mean going up onto the mountain or toward it.

decisions.choice: Kill them with stones or arrows from a distance
decisions.reason: Readable says why no hand may touch the offender. "Them" refers to "that person".

records.source: וַיֵּ֧רֶד מֹשֶׁ֛ה מִן־הָהָ֖ר אֶל־הָעָ֑ם וַיְקַדֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וַֽיְכַבְּס֖וּ שִׂמְלֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And went down Moses from the mountain to the people and he consecrated the people, and they washed their clothes.
pieces: Moses went down from the mountain to the people. He made them ready by consecrating them, and they washed their clothing.

L.14: And Moses went down from the mountain to the people, and he consecrated the people, and they washed their garments.

R.14: Moses went down the mountain to the people. He made them holy, and they washed their clothes.

decisions.choice: he consecrated the people, and they washed: Moses does what verse 10 commanded
decisions.reason: Moses carries out God's word exactly, and the people do their part. The consecrating and the washing belong together as one act of preparation.

decisions.choice: made them holy
decisions.reason: Readable uses "make holy" for "consecrate", as in verse 10.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם הֱי֥וּ נְכֹנִ֖ים לִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים אַֽל־תִּגְּשׁ֖וּ אֶל־אִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And he said to the people, be prepared for three days; do not draw near to a woman.
pieces: Moses told the people, "Be ready in three days' time. Until then, no man is to have sexual relations with a woman."

L.15: And he said to the people, "Be prepared for three days; do not draw near to a woman."

R.15: Moses told the people, "Get ready for the third day. Until then, the men must not sleep with any woman."

decisions.choice: for three days: by the third day
decisions.reason: The phrase points to the day named in verses 11 and 16: the people are to be ready on the third day.

decisions.choice: do not draw near to a woman: do not have sexual relations
decisions.reason: To "draw near to" a woman is a polite way of speaking of sexual relations (Leviticus 18:6; Isaiah 8:3). The command is spoken to the men as heads of households. Sexual relations made a person unclean until evening (Leviticus 15:18); keeping apart is part of being ready to meet God (1 Samuel 21:5-6). It says nothing against marriage itself.

decisions.choice: Moses ... Until then ... no man / the men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Moses as the speaker and say plainly what the idiom means and how long it lasts. The command is to the men, so there is no inclusive wording.

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֜י בִּֽהְיֹ֣ת הַבֹּ֗קֶר וַיְהִי֩ קֹלֹ֨ת וּבְרָקִ֜ים וְעָנָ֤ן כָּבֵד֙ עַל־הָהָ֔ר וְקֹ֥ל שֹׁפָ֖ר חָזָ֣ק מְאֹ֑ד וַיֶּחֱרַ֥ד כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was on the day the third when was the morning, and it was thunders and lightnings and a cloud heavy on the mountain and [the] sound of a ram's horn strong very, and trembled all the people who [were] in the camp.
pieces: When morning came on the third day, thunder crashed and lightning flashed. A heavy cloud lay on the mountain, and the ram's horn blew very loudly. Everyone in the camp shook with fear.

L.16: And it was on the third day, when it was morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a heavy cloud upon the mountain, and the sound of a ram's horn, very strong; and all the people who [were] in the camp trembled.

R.16: On the morning of the third day, there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, and a ram's horn blew very loud. Everyone in the camp trembled with fear.

decisions.choice: thunders ... the sound: the same word, "voices"
decisions.reason: The word for "thunders" is the plural of the word for "voice" or "sound", used again for the horn's sound in this verse and for God's answer in verse 19. The scene is full of sound.

decisions.choice: a ram's horn: a horn blown as a signal, here with no human player named
decisions.reason: The horn is a ram's horn, not the metal trumpets of Numbers 10:2. No one is said to blow it; the sound comes from the mountain, with God's coming.

decisions.choice: trembled: shook with fear
decisions.reason: The verb is used of shaking in terror (Genesis 27:33; 1 Samuel 14:15). In verse 18 the same verb is used of the mountain.

records.source: וַיּוֹצֵ֨א מֹשֶׁ֧ה אֶת־הָעָ֛ם לִקְרַ֥את הָֽאֱלֹהִ֖ים מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיִּֽתְיַצְּב֖וּ בְּתַחְתִּ֥ית הָהָֽר׃
records.gloss: And brought out Moses the people to meet the God from the camp, and they stationed themselves at [the] lower part of the mountain.
pieces: Moses brought the people out from the camp to meet God, and they took up their places below the mountain.

L.17: And Moses brought the people out to meet God from the camp, and they stationed themselves at the lower part of the mountain.

R.17: Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God. They gathered at the bottom of the mountain.

decisions.choice: to meet God: the people come to an appointed meeting
decisions.reason: The verb is used of going to meet someone who is coming. Deuteronomy 4:10 calls this "the day of the assembly" (9:10; 18:16).

decisions.choice: stationed themselves at the lower part: took their places at the foot, inside the limit
decisions.reason: The verb means to take a stand or position. The people stand at the foot of the mountain, at the limit set in verse 12.

records.source: וְהַ֤ר סִינַי֙ עָשַׁ֣ן כֻּלּ֔וֹ מִ֠פְּנֵי אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרַ֥ד עָלָ֛יו יְהוָ֖ה בָּאֵ֑שׁ וַיַּ֤עַל עֲשָׁנוֹ֙ כְּעֶ֣שֶׁן הַכִּבְשָׁ֔ן וַיֶּחֱרַ֥ד כָּל־הָהָ֖ר מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And Mount Sinai was smoking all of it, because that had come down on it Yahweh in fire; and went up its smoke like [the] smoke of the kiln, and trembled all the mountain greatly.
pieces: All of Mount Sinai was smoking, since {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had come down upon it in fire. Its smoke went up like the smoke rising from a kiln, and the entire mountain shook with great force.

L.18: And Mount Sinai was smoking, all of it, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had come down upon it in fire; and its smoke went up like the smoke of the kiln, and the whole mountain trembled greatly.

R.18: Mount Sinai was full of smoke, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had come down on it in fire. The smoke rose up like smoke from a huge oven, and the whole mountain shook hard.

decisions.choice: had come down upon it in fire: the fire and smoke are signs of God's presence
decisions.reason: God appeared to Moses in fire at the bush on this mountain (3:2), and led Israel by a pillar of fire (13:21). Deuteronomy 4:11-12 and 5:22-24 recall the fire on the mountain.

decisions.choice: kiln: a furnace for firing pottery or bricks, or for smelting
decisions.reason: The same picture is used of the smoke over Sodom (Genesis 19:28). The smoke is thick and rising in a column.

decisions.choice: the whole mountain trembled: the reading of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text says the mountain shook. The Greek translation (the Septuagint) reads that all the people were amazed, and a few Hebrew manuscripts read "all the people", as in verse 16. The Hebrew reading fits the picture of God coming down on the mountain (Judges 5:5; Psalm 68:9).

decisions.choice: a huge oven
decisions.reason: Readable says "huge oven" for "kiln", a word many readers do not know.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ ק֣וֹל הַשּׁוֹפָ֔ר הוֹלֵ֖ךְ וְחָזֵ֣ק מְאֹ֑ד מֹשֶׁ֣ה יְדַבֵּ֔ר וְהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יַעֲנֶ֥נּוּ בְקֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And it was [the] sound of the ram's horn going and strong very; Moses spoke and the God answered him with a voice.
pieces: The sound of the ram's horn kept growing stronger and stronger. Moses would speak, and God would answer him with a voice like thunder.

L.19: And the sound of the ram's horn was going on and growing very strong; Moses would speak, and God would answer him with a voice.

R.19: The ram's horn kept getting louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice that sounded like thunder.

decisions.choice: going and strong: growing steadily louder
decisions.reason: The verb "going" with another word describes something that keeps on increasing (Genesis 26:13; 2 Samuel 3:1).

decisions.choice: answered him with a voice: answered in a sound that was both voice and thunder
alternatives: God answered him with spoken words
decisions.reason: The word can mean a voice or thunder (verse 16). God may have answered Moses with words that the people heard (verse 9; Deuteronomy 4:12, 36), or in thunder that showed his answer. Both may be meant: a voice heard as thunder.

decisions.choice: Moses would speak, and God would answer: speaking that went on over time
decisions.reason: The verbs may describe repeated speaking and answering. The content is not given here; it may lead into the exchange of verses 20-24.

decisions.choice: with a voice like thunder / that sounded like thunder
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep both senses of the word, voice and thunder, together.

records.source: וַיֵּ֧רֶד יְהוָ֛ה עַל־הַ֥ר סִינַ֖י אֶל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֑ר וַיִּקְרָ֨א יְהוָ֧ה לְמֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶל־רֹ֥אשׁ הָהָ֖ר וַיַּ֥עַל מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And came down Yahweh on Mount Sinai to [the] top of the mountain, and summoned Yahweh Moses to [the] top of the mountain, and went up Moses.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came down on Mount Sinai, onto the mountain's summit, and called Moses up to the summit. So Moses went up.

L.20: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came down upon Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.

R.20: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came down to the top of Mount Sinai. He called Moses to come up to the top, and Moses went up.

decisions.choice: came down ... to the top of the mountain: a fuller telling of verse 18
decisions.reason: Verse 18 has already said that God came down on the mountain. This verse goes back over the event and adds where he came, the summit, so that Moses can be called up.

decisions.choice: called Moses ... and Moses went up: Moses alone goes near
decisions.reason: The people stay below, but Moses is called to the top. He acts as the one who goes between God and the people (20:19-21).

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה רֵ֖ד הָעֵ֣ד בָּעָ֑ם פֶּן־יֶהֶרְס֤וּ אֶל־יְהוָה֙ לִרְא֔וֹת וְנָפַ֥ל מִמֶּ֖נּוּ רָֽב׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, go down, warn the people lest they break through to Yahweh to see, and fall from it many.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go down and give the people a strict warning, so that they do not push past the boundary toward {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to gaze, and many of them fall dead.

L.21: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to see, and many of them fall.

R.21: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go down and warn the people. They must not cross the line to come and stare at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. If they do, many of them will die.

decisions.choice: warn: charge solemnly, as before witnesses
decisions.reason: The verb means to bear witness, and so to warn in the strongest terms (Genesis 43:3; Deuteronomy 8:19).

decisions.choice: break through to Yahweh to see: force past the limit to look at God
decisions.reason: The danger is that curiosity will draw the people past the limit to gaze at God's presence. To look on God carelessly brings death (33:20; Numbers 4:20; 1 Samuel 6:19).

decisions.choice: many of them fall: many will die
decisions.reason: "Fall" here means to fall dead, as in 32:28.

records.source: וְגַ֧ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים הַנִּגָּשִׁ֥ים אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה יִתְקַדָּ֑שׁוּ פֶּן־יִפְרֹ֥ץ בָּהֶ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And also the priests who draw near to Yahweh, they will consecrate themselves, lest break out against them Yahweh.
pieces: And the priests who come near to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} must also consecrate themselves, so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not burst out against them."

L.22: And also the priests who draw near to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shall consecrate themselves, lest {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} break out against them."

R.22: Even the priests who come close to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} must make themselves holy. If they do not, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike them down."

decisions.choice: the priests who draw near: those who already served as priests
decisions.reason: Aaron and his sons are not ordained until later (chapters 28-29; Leviticus 8). These priests may be men who offered sacrifice for their families before then, as the young men do in 24:5. The text does not say who they were.

decisions.choice: break out against them: strike suddenly with death
decisions.reason: The verb means to burst through. It is used of God's sudden judgment when holy things are treated wrongly (2 Samuel 6:7-8). It answers to the people's "breaking through" in verse 21.

decisions.choice: strike them down
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "break out against them" means here.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה לֹא־יוּכַ֣ל הָעָ֔ם לַעֲלֹ֖ת אֶל־הַ֣ר סִינָ֑י כִּֽי־אַתָּ֞ה הַעֵדֹ֤תָה בָּ֨נוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַגְבֵּ֥ל אֶת־הָהָ֖ר וְקִדַּשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to Yahweh, not are able the people to go up to Mount Sinai, for you you warned us saying, set bounds [for] the mountain and consecrate it.
pieces: Moses answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "There is no way the people can climb Mount Sinai. You gave us a warning: 'Mark out a boundary around the mountain and treat it as holy.'"

L.23: And Moses said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "The people are not able to go up to Mount Sinai, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} warned us, saying, 'Set bounds for the mountain and consecrate it.'"

R.23: Moses said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "The people cannot come up the mountain. You already warned us. You told us to mark a line around the mountain and to keep it holy."

decisions.choice: the people are not able: the people will not come up, because of the warning already given
alternatives: the people may not go up
decisions.reason: Moses means that the limit is already in place and the people know it. God's reply in verse 24 shows the warning must still be given again.

decisions.choice: set bounds for the mountain and consecrate it: mark the mountain off as holy
decisions.reason: To consecrate the mountain is to treat it as set apart for God, so that no one may enter it. Moses sums up verse 12, where the bounds were set "for the people": the same limit both marks the mountain and holds the people back.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֤יו יְהוָה֙ לֶךְ־רֵ֔ד וְעָלִ֥יתָ אַתָּ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹ֣ן עִמָּ֑ךְ וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהָעָ֗ם אַל־יֶֽהֶרְס֛וּ לַעֲלֹ֥ת אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה פֶּן־יִפְרָץ־בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And said to him Yahweh, go, go down, and you will come up, you and Aaron with you; and the priests and the people not let them break through to go up to Yahweh, lest he break out against them.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered him, "Go back down, and then return, you and Aaron with you. As for the priests and the people, they are not to push through to come up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, or {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will burst out against them."

L.24: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Go, go down, and you shall come up, you and Aaron with you; but the priests and the people, let them not break through to come up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, lest {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} break out against them."

R.24: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Go down and then come back up with Aaron. But do not let the priests or the people cross the line to come up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. If they do, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will strike them down."

decisions.choice: go, go down, and come up: go down now, and later come up again with Aaron
decisions.reason: The two commands "go" and "go down" are urgent: God sends Moses down despite his answer. The coming up with Aaron is for a later time; in 24:1, 9 Aaron goes up with Moses and the elders.

decisions.choice: the priests and the people: neither group may pass the limit
decisions.reason: Even the priests, who have been told to consecrate themselves (verse 22), may not go up. Only Moses, and later Aaron, are called.

records.source: וַיֵּ֥רֶד מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־הָעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲלֵהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And went down Moses to the people and he said to them.
pieces: Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.

L.25: And Moses went down to the people and said to them.

R.25: Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.

decisions.choice: and said to them: what Moses said is not given, or it is the warning of verses 21-24
alternatives: and told them (the warning of verses 21-24)
and said to them (what follows in chapter 20)
decisions.reason: The verb usually leads into the words spoken, but none follow; 20:1 begins "And God spoke all these words." Moses may have told the people the warning of verses 21-24, and the narrative then turns to God's own words in chapter 20. The Ten Words could be taken as what Moses said to them, but 20:1 and 20:19-22 present them as God's own speech.

decisions.choice: spoke to them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the open ending of the Hebrew rather than supply what Moses said.
